stories.headline: Three Dead, Including 2-Year-Old Among Injured, in Mass Shooting at Seattle Center Festival
stories.summary:
A mass shooting erupted Sunday evening at Seattle Center during the Bite of Seattle food festival, leaving three people dead and at least five others injured, including a 2-year-old boy. Police and emergency crews responded shortly after 6 p.m. local time; the venue was packed with festival-goers when gunfire broke out, sending crowds running and climbing over one another to escape.

Witnesses described scenes of chaos inside and around the Seattle Center Armory. Kayla Carris, 22, said people began screaming and rushing inside for cover, while Todd Behrends, 59, reported hearing multiple rounds of gunfire and seeing a woman on the ground and a man on a stretcher as he fled. Seattle Police urged the public to avoid the area as the investigation unfolded.

As of the initial reports, police had not confirmed whether any suspects were taken into custody. The shooting drew immediate attention given its occurrence at a major public outdoor event in a densely crowded urban setting. The incident is among the deadliest mass shootings in Seattle's recent history.

stories.headline: Update: Netanyahu Flies to U.S., Plans UN General Assembly Attendance Despite Mamdani Arrest Threat
stories.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu departed for the United States on Monday for meetings with President Trump at the White House on Tuesday and attendance at a funeral service for the late Senator Lindsey Graham. He told Fox News on Sunday that he is "not concerned" about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's earlier pledge to enforce an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him, saying Mamdani was "fomenting hate" and turning New Yorkers against one another.

Netanyahu announced he intends to attend the UN General Assembly in New York this autumn, despite the diplomatic friction with Mamdani. Last week, Mamdani acknowledged his administration lacked independent legal authority to enforce the ICC warrant but called Netanyahu a "war criminal" and urged the federal government to make the arrest. New York is not on Netanyahu's itinerary for the current visit.

The episode has sharpened debate within the Democratic Party over Israel policy. Supporters of Mamdani argue his position reflects legitimate accountability for alleged war crimes in Gaza, where over 73,000 people have been killed according to the Hamas-run health ministry — figures the UN considers reliable. Critics, including Netanyahu, contend the mayor's rhetoric has inflamed antisemitism and created a climate of fear for Jewish New Yorkers, citing a hate-crime stabbing incident in the city last week in which a Jewish man and an Asian man were attacked.

stories.headline: Andrea Pirlo Withdraws as Italy National Team Coach Candidate Over Russian Betting Firm Ties
stories.summary:
Andrea Pirlo, the former AC Milan, Juventus, and Italian national team midfielder, announced Monday he is withdrawing his candidacy to become Italy's next head coach following a backlash over his role as global ambassador for Fonbet, a Russian betting company with ties to pro-Kremlin events. His appointment had been widely reported as all but certain before the controversy emerged.

Politicians from multiple Italian parties criticized the Italian Football Federation's selection, citing Pirlo's appearances at Fonbet-sponsored events in Moscow — including one at Luzhniki Stadium that took place the same day as a major Russian strike on Ukraine. Nationalist pro-Kremlin figures, including a pop star who has openly supported the invasion of Ukraine, appeared at the same event. European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno called for an "ethical revolution" in Italian football.

Pirlo denied any political intent, writing on Instagram that his commercial work in Dubai was "exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature" and that assigning political meaning to it attributed beliefs he had never expressed. The Russian ambassador in Rome offered Pirlo support, calling his withdrawal "saddening." The controversy now risks drawing scrutiny to new FIGC technical director Paolo Maldini over similar questions.

stories.headline: India's Youth Protest Movement Claims Rare Cabinet Scalp, Vows to Press Broader Demands
stories.summary:
India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned Saturday following more than a week of sustained nationwide street protests, marking only the second cabinet resignation in twelve years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government. The protests were triggered by the cancellation of NEET, India's major medical entrance exam, after a question paper leak forced nearly two million students to retake the test; more than 20 students died by suicide, with families blaming the scandal.

The movement was organized largely through social media, particularly Instagram, bypassing the mainstream media and WhatsApp channels the government had relied on to shape public opinion. Protest momentum surged after Delhi police forcibly removed and hospitalized hunger-striking educator Sonam Wangchuk on July 18, with subsequent baton charges, tear gas, and pellet gun footage spreading rapidly online and swelling participation rather than suppressing it.

Activists and student organizers say the resignation is a beginning, not an endpoint, with calls for broader education reform and compensation for bereaved families still unresolved. The episode has been widely interpreted as the first significant demonstration that India's Gen Z can force accountability from the Modi administration through decentralized, digital-first organizing — a dynamic political analysts say could have lasting implications ahead of future elections.

stories.headline: Update: European Wildfire Crisis Deepens as 220,000 Evacuated Near Bordeaux
stories.summary:
A catastrophic wildfire in France's Gironde region forced an additional 55,000 people from their homes overnight Sunday, bringing the regional evacuation total to 220,000 as flames advanced toward the city of Bordeaux. The blaze has consumed approximately 42,000 hectares — an area four times the size of Paris — since igniting midweek, with authorities describing the fire as generating its own winds and behaving unpredictably.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez described another "difficult night" for crews battling the blaze, noting it had become "extremely virulent" before calming by dawn. Some 2,500 firefighters, 18 aircraft, soldiers, and resources from other European nations are deployed. At least 75 firefighters have been treated for injuries, and hundreds of homes have been destroyed.

Neighboring Spain is also managing wildfire evacuations along its eastern coast. Pope Leo XIV referenced the disasters at his Sunday Angelus prayer, expressing solidarity with those affected. The fires are fueled by successive heat waves that have left forests and scrubland tinder-dry across the region.

stories.headline: Argentina-Brazil Diplomatic Crisis Erupts After Milei Calls Lula 'Thief' and 'Convict' at Rally
stories.summary:
Brazil recalled its ambassador to Argentina on Sunday after Argentine President Javier Milei appeared at a campaign rally in São Paulo and publicly referred to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as "the thief" and "the convict," alluding to Lula's imprisonment before his corruption convictions were annulled. Milei was in Brazil to support Flávio Bolsonaro, son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is running against Lula in October's presidential election.

Milei also called Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes — who presided over Jair Bolsonaro's trial — "bald trash," without naming him directly. Brazilian diplomats condemned the remarks, with one source telling AFP that Milei had "insulted two branches of government, the Brazilian people and Brazilian democracy." President Lula, without naming Milei directly, told supporters that "in Brazil, we do not accept anyone sticking their nose where it doesn't belong."

The dispute marks a serious deterioration in relations between the two countries, which are each other's largest trading partners. Milei is a close political ally of the Bolsonaro family and has a track record of confrontational rhetoric toward left-wing governments in Latin America. Brazil's October presidential election is expected to be highly competitive, with Lula leading polls but over 10 percent of voters still undecided.

stories.headline: Typhoon Noul Makes Landfall in Southern China, Cancels Hundreds of Hong Kong Flights
stories.summary:
Typhoon Noul, described by Chinese state media as the strongest typhoon to make landfall in China so far in 2026, struck southern China on Sunday morning, bringing powerful winds and heavy rain across the region. Hong Kong's airport cancelled approximately 360 passenger flights as the storm passed, and police responded to numerous calls after multi-storey scaffolding collapsed along a major road in the Cheung Sha Wan district. No injuries from the scaffolding collapse were immediately reported.

The storm's landfall disrupted transport and infrastructure across the region. Typhoon Noul is the most significant storm system to hit the Chinese mainland this year, according to official Chinese media, underscoring the intensity of the 2026 typhoon season as it enters its peak months.

stories.headline: Australian Court Upholds Racial Discrimination Ruling Against Senator Pauline Hanson
stories.summary:
Australia's Federal Court has upheld a 2024 ruling that One Nation party leader Pauline Hanson racially discriminated against Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi in a 2022 social media post in which she told the Muslim senator to "go back" to Pakistan. Justice Melissa Perry dismissed Hanson's appeal on Monday, rejecting her argument that the post constituted protected political communication. The original ruling found the post was "a variant of the slogan 'go back to where you came from,'" a phrase deemed a racist trope targeting Muslims.

Faruqi, who brought the case under Australia's Racial Discrimination Act, said outside court that "today's win is for every single person who has been made to feel that their belonging in this country is conditional." The original judgment ordered Hanson to delete the tweet and pay Faruqi's legal costs. Hanson said she was "disappointed" and would review the decision with her legal team "with a view to commencing an appeal in the High Court of Australia."

The case has drawn significant attention given Hanson's long history of controversial statements about Muslim immigration, including past advocacy for a "Muslim ban." The ruling tests the boundaries between political speech and racial vilification under Australian law, a question with broad implications for public discourse in the country.
